perspective:
Mason’s available information:

- He is an accountant at a small community center. Martha Moua is his colleague there, a personal care aide. Their relationship is professional and not close.
- He personally reviewed financial reports and saw discrepancies: healthcare expenses seemed unusually high compared with usual spending. This made him suspicious and anxious that Martha might be mismanaging funds.
- He initiated a conversation with Martha, saying the numbers did not add up and pointing to the healthcare-expense section. He heard Martha say there might have been a misentry and that she would review and correct any errors.
- After reviewing the report with Martha, he understood the discrepancies were due to a simple clerical error, not mismanagement. He felt relieved and embarrassed. He heard Martha say errors happen, it was okay, she understood he was being thorough, and they should double-check entries next time. He apologized for his initial suspicion.
- He then believed Martha was competent and that the recurring clerical errors meant the financial management system was inadequate. He felt frustrated with the system but empathetic toward Martha. He told Martha the issue was not her management but the system, suggested a new, more robust financial system, and said he would draft a proposal for her input. He heard Martha agree and offer to help.
- He finished drafting the new financial system proposal. He believed it would benefit operations but was unsure how management would receive it. He heard Martha call it solid and encourage confidence. He said he would prepare a detailed presentation and asked Martha to help gather data; she agreed.
- He presented the proposal to management. He felt satisfied with his effort but physically and mentally exhausted, believing he had done everything possible; the decision now rested with management. He heard Martha praise his work, suggest taking time off, and offer help while he was away. He thanked her and planned to take a few days off to recharge, reflect, and hope for good news.

Not available to Mason: management’s private decision or deliberations, Martha’s private thoughts or feelings beyond what she expressed, any hidden events, and narrator-only details about other characters.
